visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with brown hair, wearing a white shirt and colorful drop earrings, sits on a grey couch. A Pikachu plushie and a Harry Potter themed pillow are visible behind her. Large yellow text with a black outline appears on screen. (2) Close-up shot of a black smartphone held in hands. The screen shows an Instagram profile and a specific photo post. Finger gestures demonstrate navigation and taking screenshots of UI elements. (3) The phone screen shows the Instagram Story editor interface. The user interacts with image overlays, enlarging a shared post and positioning cropped rectangular bars at the top and bottom. (4) The user switches to the iOS Photos app. A finger long-presses on a person in a photo, causing a white glow effect to outline the subject, indicating the 'lift subject' feature. (5) Returning to the Instagram Story interface, the user pastes the cutout person and carefully drags it to align with the background image. (6) A brief cutaway shows a digital video of three men sitting at a desk with microphones, looking surprised. (7) The woman is back on screen, holding her phone to show the finished story. She taps the screen to demonstrate the link functionality, then smiles and gestures with her hands as she continues to speak. Yellow captions appear at the bottom throughout.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Hook -> Sequence of Instructional Steps -> Demonstration of Result -> Conclusion.
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video is a practical tutorial teaching viewers how to use a multi-layered design trick on Instagram Stories. By combining screenshots, post-sharing, and the iPhone's automatic image cutout feature, the creator shows how to make a shared post look like a high-quality layered graphic while maintaining its interactive functionality.
